summary: Checked the GitHub Pages submodule fix. HEAD and the index have no 160000 gitlink entries. There is no .gitmodules, cybconf/.git or cybconf/.github. All 339 cybconf files are tracked as normal files, including _config.yml, Gemfile, Gemfile.lock and index.html. _site, .jekyll-cache and the zips are not tracked. .github/workflows/jekyll.yml is tracked, parses as valid YAML, has build and deploy jobs with deploy needing build, uses working-directory cybconf and uploads cybconf/_site. In a fresh `git clone /app` into /tmp (no commits to /app), `bundle install` plus `JEKYLL_ENV=production bundle exec jekyll build --baseurl /pp` succeeded and produced _site/index.html and 14 HTML pages. The live preview initially did NOT work: the container had restarted, and the gems installed with `gem install` (bundler 2.6.9, jekyll and the rest) were gone, so supervisor frontend was FATAL with 'bundle: not found'. I reinstalled bundler 2.6.9, ran bundle install and restarted frontend. After that, home and /call-for-papers/ return 200. 9/9 pytest pass.

ui_bugs.issue: Breaks after every container wakeup. The Ruby gems are installed system-wide (/var/lib/gems, /usr/local/bin/bundle), and that location does not persist. Only the ruby-full apt package is replayed from /app/.emergent/system_deps.txt. I restored it manually this time.

ui_bugs.component: CSS backgrounds on GitHub Pages project site
ui_bugs.issue: The remote is github.com/Ronden1234/pp, so Pages serves under /pp and the workflow passes --baseurl /pp. assets/css/custom-index.css:604 (contact hero, url('/assets/images_26/imgs/contact.webp')) and assets/css/program.css:32 (url("/assets/images_26/imgs/unical_start.webp")) use root-absolute URLs, so these backgrounds will 404 on the deployed site. HTML links use relative_url and are fine.

action_items: Make the preview survive restarts: install gems into the repo (bundle config set --local path vendor/bundle in /app/cybconf; cybconf/vendor/ is already gitignored). Make the start script install bundler if needed and run `bundle install` before `jekyll serve`, e.g. "gem list -i bundler -v 2.6.9 || gem install bundler -v 2.6.9; cd /app/cybconf && bundle install && bundle exec jekyll serve ...".
Change the root-absolute url('/assets/...') in custom-index.css:604 and program.css:32 to relative paths (e.g. url('../images_26/imgs/contact.webp')) so they work under the /pp baseurl.

Optional: _config.yml url is https://cybconf-ieee-2027.github.io/, which does not match the actual Pages host (ronden1234.github.io/pp). absolute_url, the feed and SEO links will point to the wrong host. Either rename the repo or org, or update the url / pass --baseurl/url in CI.
critical_code_review_comments: Gemfile.lock PLATFORMS includes x86_64-linux, but there are no x86_64-linux variants of google-protobuf, sass-embedded or ffi. CI will fall back to the ruby-platform gems and compile them, which works but is slower. It built fine here on aarch64 the same way. Optional: run `bundle lock --add-platform x86_64-linux` with network access for prebuilt gems.
The workflow triggers only on the 'main' branch. Make sure the user pushes to main, and set Pages Source to 'GitHub Actions' in the repo settings, otherwise the legacy Pages build may still run.
BUNDLED WITH 2.5.7 in Gemfile.lock while 2.6.9 is used locally. This is harmless; setup-ruby will install 2.5.7.

success_rate.backend: 100% (9/9 after restoring the gems for the preview)

seed_data_creation: none. Temp clones are in /tmp/clonetest and pytest tmp_path. Clone gems are in /tmp/clonevendor. Nothing was committed to /app.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run `python -m pytest /app/tests/test_pages_repo_build.py -v`. If the preview is down after a wakeup, check `sudo supervisorctl status frontend` and look for 'bundle: not found'. Gems are not persisted.
rca of the issue: Preview failure: the container restart wiped the system gem dir. supervisor frontend runs `yarn start`, which runs `bundle exec jekyll serve`, so it exits 127 and goes FATAL. Fix: install the gems to vendor/bundle inside /app and bootstrap bundler in the start script.
